newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 17.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Selected members of the cabinet agreed on a general outline of the Czech national defence plan.

- The majority owner of Poldi Ocel, Vladimir Stehlik has given up all functions in the foundery, including the chairmanship of the supervisory council of the newly formed Poldi Steel, according to Stehlik's legal representative, Jiri Teryngel.

- Following McDonnell Douglas's recent offer to cooperate with Aero Vodochody, Boeing has also confirmed its interest in the largest Czech aeroplane manufacturer. According to the president of Czech Airlines (CSA), both CSA and Boeing are interested in splitting a total of approximately 35 percent of the company.

- The Ministry of Industry and Trade is preparing a decree which will prohibit any company other than the state-owned Transgas from importing natural gas into the country. Any company has had the right to request a license to import gas until now.

- The government will discuss the budget for the National Property Fund during its sitting today. The cost of operating the fund should be 170 million crowns in 1997, an increase of six percent from 1996.
- Czech Airlines is increasing the price of its airline tickets by 3 percent effective January 1.

- RadioMobil announced that the extension of its mobile telephone network will be delayed by three months. RadioMobil's services are currently available to approximately 30 percent of the country's inhabitants.

- The number of small banks in the Czech Republic will likely decrease by 10 in 1997, according to the general manager of Ceska Sporitelna, Jaroslav Klapal. Until now five banks have lost their licenses and six are currently under forced administration.

PRAVO - The current helthcare situation is very serious according to 90 percent of Czech doctors. A poll indicates that one third of Czech doctors believe that the helthcare system will collapse if there are no solutions found in the near future.

- While the price of crude oil has decreased with the anticipated influx of Iraqi oil, the price of petrol and diesel will likely not decrease, according to the spokesman from Ceska Rafinerska, Ales Soukup.

- The Czech National Bank is currently discussing the conditions of participating in the central bank's preventative programme for small and medium-sized banks with six banks, according to a spokesman for the central bank, Martin Svehla.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Ministry of Finance implemented forced administration against the CNIS investment company, according to Jan Veverka from the ministry. -- Prague Newsroom, +42-2-2423-0003
